And the fact is you have no idea why these people went to Banja Luka, do you?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know the specific reason why they went to Banja Luka but I knew that they were going to Banja Luka. That's my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's all I have, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was just going to check because he did also explain on Friday, more or less along the same lines as he did today, that they found it strange at the time that they would go to Banja Luka -- that they would go to Banja Luka and not Zenica. I was trying to find it but if there are no further questions, I think we can leave it at that. Sir, that brings us to the end of your testimony. As Presiding Judge in this trial, me in my own name and on behalf of the other two Judges, Judge Janu from the Czech Republic and Judge Taya from Japan and also on behalf of the Tribunal, I would like to thank you for coming over to give evidence. You will be escorted from the courtroom by the usher and you will be given all the assistance you require to enable you to return to your country of residence. Should you encounter any difficulties, please let us know. On our part we wish you a safe journey back home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, I take it Madam Richterova that the next witness is here?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The next witness is here but because with this witness we will start a new municipality, I would like to deal with Rule 92 bis for the witnesses from Donji Vakuf municipality. We received a reply from the Defence regarding the witness 7.164.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I need to get the document, appropriate document, to be able to follow you here. 7.164? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And we didn't receive any reply for the Witness 7.153. However, Mr. Ackerman informed me orally that he doesn't object to using his statement under the Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Saving his general reservations on Rule 92?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I actually prepared two documents, a first response and a second response, and sent them for filing but for some reason only the second response got filed. I will resubmit the first response so that it gets in the record and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: -- my position on it. But Ms. Richterova is correct. I do not have an opposition other than what I normally say in those responses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know. I take it that this is so. So all right. So I think there is no problems as far as that is concerned. You can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would like to tender these two statements into evidence, if you allow us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And again, Your Honour, I have no objection beyond that general objection that I put in all these responses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So the documents -- the statements are being admitted under the Rule 92 rule, under Rule 92 and they are given exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness 7.153 was given Exhibit number P1694, and the witness statement 7.164 was given an exhibit number P1695.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. All right. So that's done.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And I'm sorry to bring one other thing but it relates to Rule 92 bis as well, and it relates to the witness 7.263. It is witness from -- I know, it is witness who was supposed to testify about three weeks ago. The witness didn't appear. We would like to ask -- this witness testified in Stakic case, and we would like to ask the Defence whether he would agree to accept this -- the transcript under Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I've already talked to Ms. Richterova about this and made it real clear that I would not accept the transcript. That there is significant cross-examination with regard to this witness, and it does go directly to the conduct of the accused, so it doesn't fall under Rule 92 bis in the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you. It's true we discussed it. I just wanted to have it on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So do you -- yeah, but as a result of the opposition that you have now do you stick to your request or do you withdraw it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We will withdraw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So that goes on the record as well, because it's the most important part of this story. Next?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And the witness is ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So usher, please -- does this witness -- this witness does not enjoy any -- as far as I can recall from my records, he does not enjoy any protective measures, no?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No, he wasn't asking for any protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And how long do you anticipate to examine him in-chief for?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, already knows me that I anticipate always shorter time. I want to hope that I will manage to finish him today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which would mean tomorrow will be reserved for cross-examination and tomorrow, apart from this witness, do you have any other witness? I wouldn't think so?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No, we don't have. We already announced that the major witness will testify from Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Madam Chuqing, I think that clarifies more what I have handed down to you in writing so the planning is more or less along these lines. Yes. Where is the witness? Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Odobasic. And welcome to this Tribunal. You are a lawyer by profession so I will cut short my introduction. The gentleman standing next to you is the usher, he's going to hand you the text of a solemn declaration to the effect that in the course of your testimony, you'll be saying the truth, speaking the truth and nothing but the truth. Please read out that text aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us. It's the equivalent of an oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. Please sit down. And Madam Richterova, with whom I suppose you are already familiar, is going to lead the examination-in-chief on behalf of the Prosecution. Yes, Madam Richterova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, witness. Can you please state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Jasmin Odobasic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When and where were you born?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 2nd of April, 1952, in Prnjavor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your ethnic origin is Bosniak and your religion is Muslim; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You studied at the university and you graduated as a lawyer; correct?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I obtained a degree in law, and for a brief period of time, I worked as a Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: In the period of 1990 and 1991, what was your occupation?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: The year of 1990 caught me working as a general secretary of the shoe factory in Prnjavor. After I was removed from that organisation, I opened a law firm which survived only for three days when it was destroyed as a result of an explosion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We will go into details and you will have opportunity to talk about this but now please just answer my questions. I would like to show the witness a map Prnjavor municipality, and I believe that Your Honours and the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We will provide the Defence with spare copy. And I would like to tender this map into evidence under P1765.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you please just briefly discuss what was the ethnic composition of Prnjavor municipality?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: The municipality of Prnjavor was one of the most mixed municipalities in the former Yugoslavia, in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Nineteen ethnicities lived there apart from the three most numerous ones, Croats, Serbs and Muslims. There were a number of minorities, Czechs, Poles, Ukrainians, Ruthenians and so on and so forth. There were 46.000 citizens in the municipality. 71.6 per cent were Serbs, 15.3 per cent were Bosniaks, 3.7 per cent were Croats and 9.4 per cent were others. These other ethnicities, minorities, and those who declared themselves as Yugoslavs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be so kind and have a look at the map which is next to you? And we already heard that Serbs were in majority in this municipality, and Bosniaks had about 15 per cent. Were there any Muslims villages which would be purely Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were four or five villages which were exclusively Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Would you be so kind and place the map on the machine and point on the machine at these villages, please?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: As I have already said, Bosniak villages were located near the town, the villages of Konjhovci, Mravica, Galjipovci, Lisnja, Puraci and then there was a small number of Bosniaks living in the village of Bobanovci which is not on the map but which is located 2 to 3 kilometres from the Prnjavor town.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And was there any Croat village?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Croats and Bosniaks lived for the most part in the town itself but there were two other villages, the village of Drenova where the population was almost 100 per cent Croat. It is located before Donji Vijacani [phoen] on this communication line and there were also some Croats living in the village of Kulas which you can see here on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm done with the map. Witness, how would you describe, just very briefly, the life in this multi-ethnic municipality? How was the relationship between various ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: I will try to give you a brief description, though this is a demanding task, because of the extent to which this community was mixed and because of the diversity of this area. At the time of the former Yugoslavia, which existed until 1991, the life of these minorities and these three main ethnicities in the town itself was very harmonious. Minorities had schools in their own language, Italians, Ukrainians and Ruthenians, every significant minority also had their cultural societies and there was a cultural society in the town itself in which all these minorities participated. There were no conflicts whatsoever, and Prnjavor -- in Prnjavor itself there had not been any massacres during the two world wars. However, according to the stories told by elderly people, there were such attempts but people helped each other and provided shelter to each other. So in 1990s, more than one-third of marriages were mixed, and often the President of the municipality was a member of a minority community, Italian, Ukrainian, Croat, Serb, and I personally had a lot of friends amongst these minorities, Italians, Czechs and others. Which was the case with the other citizens living in this area, including Croats and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And are you able to tell us whether at some point this ideal relationship among different ethnicities changed?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: The relationship among different ethnicities started to change from the beginning of 1990s, but at the beginning, these changes seemed to have been imposed, which was the case in most of the cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When you say they seemed to have been imposed, what are you implying to?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: As I have already said, there had never been any conflicts between these ethnicities or minorities in the town itself. To illustrate this point, there had not been any murders in the area at all. There were more suicides than murders. There had been no significant incidents up until 1990. As for the changes that were imposed at one point in time, from elsewhere, I abide by what I stated. This small area was often referred to as a small Europe, a little Europe, because of the harmony, of the harmonious life of these ethnicities and minorities, and if you will allow me just one more sentence --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No. I will allow you later to elaborate but now I would like to know when and how this ideal life changed. When was it?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: It happened with the formation of national political parties. This harmonious life started to change, and I remember that it came as a big surprise, which was followed by fear in Prnjavor, when in 1989, at a rally organised by the SDS, a certain Mr. Zelenbaba declared: "Citizens you better start selling your life stock and start buying rifles and getting ready for war." People were shocked and then incidents started to occur.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Tell me which parties were formed in Prnjavor.

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: In the town itself, there was the SDP, which was a successor to the former League of Communists, a Reformist Party was also established in the town, since there was not much response, not much interest for national parties in the town itself. I think the SDS was established in the village of Strpci or Visnja, villages located outside the town, although they did hold a rally inside the town before they were formally established. So this -- this idea did not find fertile soil in the town itself. These national parties were first established outside the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And these parties, and you already touched, did they organise their own rallies? And let's start with SDS. Did they held -- did they hold any rallies, either in the town of Prnjavor or in other villages?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Before the first multi-party elections, all political parties with the exception of the reformists in the Prijedor municipality had been organising promotional rallies. I remember one such rally organised by the SDS at the main square. It was then that I saw for the first time some of the emblems from the Second World War, which had never been seen prior to that in the town itself. The SDS also held rallies in the village of Visnja and in a number of other local communes. The SDP, and I participated in their activities myself because this was the only multi-national, multi-ethnic, multi-confessional political party, held their rally at the main square, in the centre of the town, and a number of rallies in the neighbouring villages, and local communities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You already mentioned this one particular rally when Dusan Zelenbaba stated, "Serbs, you -- rather sell your live stock and by the rifles." Were you present during this rally?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: I was present at this rally. I observed what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you remember who else was present on the side of the SDS party?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: I saw Radovan Karadzic, he was present. Leaders of the Prnjavor SDS, Radan Djuric, Jovan Vasic and a number of their associates, their colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And can we be a little bit more specific about the time? You said it was before the elections. Was it in 1990?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: The first multi-party elections were held in 1990, and a month or two prior to the elections, all of the parties organised their promotional rallies. They went campaigning, recruiting activists, issued membership cards and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And during this time, are you aware of any other rallies where some nationalistic views would be introduced?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: I did not attend them because I never went outside of the town to attend those rallies. However, I know that some of the rallies, and I think in the villages of Smrtici and Strpci, there was a group of activists of the SDS that walked out, or rather the SDA walked out, although they had been invited to attend as guests. They walked out due to very fierce national statements that had been made and that had been addressed to them. I was informed of this by one of the members of that party who attended and walked out. I can give you his name, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether SDP and SDA held their own rallies as well?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: I've already told you, the SDA held their rallies in the four Muslim villages, whereas the SDP also held them in many villages and local communes. They had their pre-election rallies. I participated in some of them, although I was a member of the SDP for only two years. That was a multi-national party and this is why I had agreed to participate in these pre-election rallies. As far as these gatherings are concerned, I avoid attending them due to symbols that were used at those rallies, first and foremost by the SDS. They were using flags with skulls, with four Cs and so on. They also issued threats. And it wasn't a good idea to attend these rallies, if one knew that you favoured a different political option, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what about SDA? Did they present some symbols as well, during their rallies?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember well they used green and white flags with the SDA written on them. At least during that time, I didn't see other kinds of flags.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know what was the result of the elections in the Prnjavor municipality?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Certainly. We were interested in getting as many seats as possible, so we followed the number of seats won by each party. According to the Statute of the Prnjavor municipality, the assembly had 60 seats. SDS won 42 seats. SDP won 11. SDA won 5. And I think that the remaining two or three seats were won by the Reformist Party of Ante Markovic so the 42 seats constituted the absolute majority in the Prnjavor assembly and it was won by the SDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We need to have a break now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to have a break. 15 minutes? 15 minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead, Madam Richterova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Before we will talk about the events which occurred after the elections, I would like to ask you whether there were any paramilitary formations in Prnjavor before the elections?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Before the elections, I used to see some people bearing arms, which under normal circumstances, was banned. Most often I would see them in the villages of Kremna and in that area, meaning Luzani villages, near Vijacani and so on. However, they claimed that those people were the so-called reservists of the Yugoslav People's Army which wasn't the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And did they form any group or were they just a separate people carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: In the village of Kremna they used to meet very often and they spent time together. Now, whether they were part of a formation at the time, I couldn't tell you that. I believed that they started becoming active in 1991, as a formal unit, when they started going to the battlefields in Croatia and elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And when you now stated that they started becoming active in 1991 as a formal unit, do you know what kind of unit, what was -- whether they had any name?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: The unit was known as Wolves from Vucjak.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And did you know at that time who was their commander?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: At the time, their commander was a certain Veljko Milankovic, somebody that I know very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And when we are going back to the time of the election, elections, this group was already formed or not?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: They were armed, and I personally saw them even before the first multi-party elections, namely my party wished to hold a pre-election gathering in the village of Kremna where the base of that unit was located. We made proper announcements to the police and other organs but in front of the hall in that village we were met by armed members of the unit. Their commander said that they wouldn't allow communists to hold a pre-election gathering because they wished to hold one as well, simultaneously. A tension arose there so we decided to go some 200 to 300 metres away to a school building to healed our rally there because this man, the commander, had two or three armed members of his unit standing next to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And do you know which ethnicity were members of this armed group?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: For the most part, they were Serbs. However, there was a very small number of Bosniaks, a certain number of Croats in it as well. I don't know whether there were any other ethnicities in that unit. Perhaps there was a Ukrainian or two.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And you mentioned that this group stop you entering that building because they wanted to hold their own gatherings. Do you know which party were they referring to?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: They were all members of the SDS. Moreover, the commander of the Wolves, Veljko Milankovic, said to me, "Why are you among the communists? Go to your own national party, the SDA." I replied to him I told him that those weren't the communists, that that was the Reformist Party.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And we already heard that the elections were won by the SDS. Do you know who became the President of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Naturally, Nemanja Vasic became president of the municipality, somebody who graduated from the high school with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And do you know who became the President of the executive board?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: A certain Radivoje Radivojevic, whom I know also well because I used to be his boss.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And you also stated that some seats went to other parties. Did members of these other parties got some important position in newly established government of the Prnjavor municipality?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: We were second ranking party, based on the seats that we won. We were told that we could not be allocated any offices, and we didn't really want them. I know that the SDA received or got two lower ranking offices. Two men were appointed to those offices. One was in charge of an agency that procured firewood, took care of vehicles, electrical supply, water supply, and so on, within the municipal government. The other office was the secretariat for local communes, local administration, and the registry office. That was all. The highest offices were not awarded to any members of other parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And by any chance, do you remember who was the President of the Prnjavor municipality before Nemanja Vasic?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: I couldn't remember the name now. Let me think.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness an exhibit, P10. I can provide a copy. This is a document dated 15 of April, 1991, and it is a decision by which the municipality of Prnjavor adopts the agreement to join the Bosnian Krajina community of municipalities. And Nemanja Vasic, the President of the Prnjavor Municipal Assembly is here authorised to sign the agreement on joining the Bosnian Krajina community of municipalities on behalf of the Prnjavor municipality. Do you know or was it ever discussed in the municipality that Prnjavor would join this Bosnian Krajina community of municipalities?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: I personally didn't talk to anybody about joining it. However, one day, in the afternoon, I was at home and at the local radio, Dragan Djuric was a guest in a broadcast. He had been elected to the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the first multi-party elections. He spent some two hours, almost, explaining the reasons that led to the establishment of the Autonomous Region. He explained the goals and tasks of that region. It was a programme that was open to the public, the public could call in with questions, and I called with a question as well. Later on, I heard that that regional community had been established.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness Exhibit P61. I provided Your Honours with the copy because it wasn't in the binder. And if you would be so kind and have a look at the first page, the title is "List of Representatives in the Krajina Autonomous Region Assembly." And you can see a few names from Prnjavor Municipal Assembly. Can you just briefly tell us first whether you knew that these people were representatives from Prnjavor to the Krajina Autonomous Region Assembly?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Nemanja Vasic was president of the Municipal Assembly, therefore he was an assemblyman. The other person, Dobrivoje Vidic also was elected to the Republic Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the multi-party elections. Dragan Djuric was also elected to the Republic Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Borivoje Vasic is a peculiar kind of person. Therefore, I don't know whether he took part in the Municipal Assembly for the following reasons: He was a second-ranking person on the SDP list in the multi-party elections and since we won 11 seats, he got a seat in the assembly. Nobody else from the SDP was interested in taking part in the work of the Assembly, but I think that this gentleman, Borivoje Vasic, appeared a few days later as a secretary of the Secretariat for Economy in the Prnjavor municipality, as a member of the SDS, and I'm sure that he took part in the work of the Assembly. The following one, Mehmed Sabic, I couldn't tell you about him, whether he was a member or not, but I know that he was our man, somebody who appeared on our list in the multi-party elections. I don't know about the two following gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When you said on "our" list, which party are you referring? Are you referring to SDP?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: SDP.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And do you know what was his nationality? Ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabic was a Bosniak. He was quite inactive in the political life. I'm referring to the pre-elections period. He agreed to getting on the ticket of the SDP, and even gave a speech at a pre-election rally in Prnjavor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know whether he stayed in politics throughout 1991 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: I know that this man later on, I believe in 1993 or perhaps in 1994, fled from Prnjavor and went to Hungary. I don't know whether he was politically active and to what extent during that period of time in Prnjavor political establishment. I believe that he was not active.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the Witness Exhibit 1785.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This document has title "Summary of Information of Interest for Security in Prnjavor Municipality." And it is dated 15 of March, 1992. Mr. Odobasic, did you have opportunity to read this document?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You had this opportunity yesterday when you read your statement. I would like to ask you, does this document reflect accurately the situation in the Prnjavor municipality? It starts with the ethnic composition and I think you already stated it was a multi-ethnic municipality.

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I read this document yesterday for the first time. As to your question regarding the ethnic composition, I know that it is only somewhat different compared to the figures that I provided. My statistics come from the ethnic map of Bosnia and Herzegovina which was published by the Statistical Institute of Bosnia and Herzegovina prior to the first multi-party elections. I think that these data here are not fully accurate. I think that my data were more accurate but you can see from this, these data here, that the ethnic structure was mixed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It says -- I will ask you a question and you will answer my question, please. The first paragraph says "The SDS party won a majority of votes in the election but extremist tendencies predominate in the senior leadership of this party," and further down, when we have a title, "Evaluation by Political Parties," these people who were in politics in Prnjavor municipality are listed. Do you know -- or would you characterise the people who were elected for the SDS as extremists or not?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Some of these people I can freely characterise as extremists. Some were more moderate, to a certain extent. However, as regards the top leadership, almost 100 per cent of them were extremists, but I can also talk about them individually.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When you say the top leadership, and you are referring to SDS top leadership in Prnjavor; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Of course, the SDS leadership and the people appointed by the SDS to individual offices within the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us very briefly just the names, who was among these top SDS leadership in Prnjavor?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can give you a number of names. Nemanja Vasic, for instance, Dragan Djuric, Dobrivoje Vidic, three Cvijetic brothers, Pero Turudija, Pero Rudonjic, Milan Spasojevic, Radivoje Radivojevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We already talked about Nemanja Vasic as the President of the municipality. Can you really very briefly describe the behaviour of this person in 1991 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: It would be very difficult to describe his behaviour briefly but I'll do my best. As I have said, I know the gentleman because we went to school together. We went together to the university after that, and I know that after that, while he was employed at the Autoprevoz company where he was manager for a while, he was a communist, an extreme communist, and persecuted people who were not in favour of the communist idea. Shall I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No. Please I ask you about his behaviour in 1991 and 1992, and very briefly, what was his relationship with the other parties? What was his stance towards the other nationalities, another ethnicities in the municipality? How did you express his ideas, if he had any ideas?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: I must say here that prior to the period of time you're asking about, he was the front man of the Prnjavor League of Communists and at the time, he was quite extreme. After that, he moved to the SDS. He changed his attitude and his behaviour. He was amongst the first ones who started going to the church. In his speeches, he often declared that it was impossible for Muslims, Serbs and of course Croats and others to live together. He did everything he could to prevent other options. As far as I'm concerned, personally, he prevented me from carrying out the referendum in Prnjavor in 1992, and he made a number of very extremist statements in the media. He was always in the group of the most vociferous ones who held meetings around the town of Prijedor [As interpreted] and this was later reported on in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We have on the -- in the transcript around the town of Prijedor. Did you talk about the Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the witness said in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about Prnjavor all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We just have to be clear about the transcript. You stated that he made a number of very extremist statements in the media. Do you remember any of these speeches?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: I personally heard one such speech only once. I don't know whether it was in 1991 or 1992, when he said that they were not going to persecute anyone. He was referring to Muslims and Croats, with weapons, but that they would use other means, such as extortion, blackmail and other methods and he said that eventually they will leave on their own, which is what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And now can you -- you mentioned that Radivoje Radivojevic was elected as the president of the executive board. Can you very briefly describe this person and his attitude?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radivojevic is also one of the people I knew very well. He was -- I was his construction inspector in a -- the period of time between 1983 and 1987. At the time, he behaved more or less normally, except that when he attended some celebrations that we attended together. When he would criticise the existing system and glorify the old Kingdom of Yugoslavia. I know that he is from a town in Serbia by origin, where Draza Mihajlovic, one of the worst war criminals from the Second World War was born. He imitated, impersonated him, in 1991, 1992, he wore similar spectacles as Draza Mihajlovic did. He knew how to make sure that his attitude were implemented. He was the one who organised training of this formation called Wolves from Vucjak in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And how did you learn about this, that it was him who organised the training?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: I didn't observe it myself, but he organised the send-off of this paramilitary unit when they went to Knin where they stayed for about 40 days in Knin and that he organised the welcome party when they came back from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And in this document is also mentioned one Mladen Saric. Do you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: I know him very well. This was the man who was appointed director of the local radio station, Radio Prnjavor, by the SDS, after Nedjeljko Sanicin had been removed, who was closely related to Mladen because he refused to advertise the extremist attitudes of the SDS. His son at the time was working at the state television of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I mean those were the reasons why Mr. Sanicin was replaced. The first statement by Saric that I heard broadcast over the radio was something, "Brothers, the war between Serbs and Croats will be led, will go on until the last Muslim is killed."

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And another and last name which I'm interested in is Dragan Djuric. Did you know Dragan Djuric? You already mentioned that he was a representative in the Krajina Autonomous Region Assembly. What else did you know about this person?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: I didn't know him very well. We met officially a couple of occasions while I was still working for -- at the shoe factory. He was the manager of a shop and he was selling office supplies. After the attempts to establish the SDS, he became very active and involved, and apart from Nemanja Vasic, he was one of the most extreme persons in the municipality of Prnjavor. He often made very extreme statements in the BH parliament and I know the names of deputies who can confirm this. In the town itself, he often visited local companies to make sure whether -- that the remaining Croats and Muslims had been sacked. Two managers complained to me personally that he was doing this on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We will talk about this. I would like to return to this document, and I want to ask you about one thing. It is the third paragraph on the first page, and it is the third sentence, stating: "The SDA is very resentful of the Serbian authorities, partly because they are Serbian but partly for justifiable reasons because of the tactlessness of those most responsible in the executive political authority. The Muslim clergy exerts a powerful influence but here too there is a division." Can you make a comment on this? First, was the Muslim clergy -- did Muslim clergy have a powerful influence?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: This assessment, whatever its author, is really ridiculous. The Prnjavor Bosniaks were not very religious. They were hardly religious at all. I don't know whether there was an imam in the town of Prijedor [As interpreted] in at the time -- in Prnjavor town. I know, for instance, in the village of Konjhovci the local religious leader was close to the SDA because I happened to see at one of the rallies that I attended that he was actively involved in politics. As for the influence of the religion generally speaking on the population of Prnjavor, there was really very little such influence because of the fact that the population was so mixed and because the national political parties had not been organised in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we need to stop there for today.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, would it be possible to ask one more question and I am done with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I ask already about this Muslim clergy. Now, can you, and very briefly, tell us the stand, the attitude, of the SDA and SDP towards the SDS? Very briefly, 1991, 1992. And we will elaborate on that later, but now I want to hear your comment on this particular sentence.

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: The SDP operated on the basis of very firm principles. They did not cooperate with SDA or SDS in any respect. As for the relationship between the SDS and the SDA, prior to the first multi-party elections, they had met and appeared together in various programmes or rallies. Their joint position was that the communist government should be -- had to go. The SDS, however, took over, and I think that they adopted the same attitude to their former partners, including the SDP and others. They were quick to exclude all others from the political life in Prijedor [As interpreted] and the first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: In Prnjavor, interpreter apologises.

utterances.speaker: JASMIN ODOBASIC
utterances.text: After the multi-party election.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So that's the end for today. We need to stop here because our time is up. We will reconvene tomorrow in the afternoon at 2.15. Do you think between you and you, Mr. Ackerman, that you will manage to finish with there witness by tomorrow 5.00?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I will try to do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We have a pretty good chance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, good evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 4th day of March, 2003, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.36 p.m.,
